name: Shopify (Admin GraphQL API)
verdict: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard (dev.shopify.com) and pick distribution carefully because it can't be changed. Custom distribution reaches one store or one Plus org with no review, same day. Letting arbitrary merchants connect needs public distribution and App Store review, which has been running 2–6+ weeks in 2026, plus a separate protected-customer-data approval if your agent reads customer names, emails, phones or addresses.

difficulty.label: Hard
difficulty.rationale: Development and custom distribution are self-serve. The App Store path is predictable but heavy. You need a merchant-facing UI in the admin, three mandatory compliance webhooks, expiring offline tokens, Shopify Billing if you charge, and a screencast plus test credentials. Level 2 protected customer data review adds security controls. Review queues have been backlogged through 2026, with community reports of 2–5 weeks before first contact.

first_token.note: Sign up for a free Partner account, create an app in the Dev Dashboard (or with `shopify app init`), create a dev store, install the app and run the auth code grant. Protected customer fields work on dev stores once you select them in API access requests, with no review.

production.estimate: Custom distribution: same day. Public/App Store: 3–8+ weeks
production.active_effort: Custom: 1–2 h. Public: 1–3 weeks (embedded UI, compliance webhooks, billing, listing assets, screencast, PCD data-protection answers)
production.waiting: App Store review: officially 'up to 2 weeks', but community reports in 2026 run 2–5+ weeks, and each fix-and-resubmit can add more. Protected customer data review is part of the same submission.
production.note: The wait is driven by the App Review queue (backlogged since early 2026 per Shopify staff), resubmission cycles (resubmitting sends you to the back of the queue), and Level 2 PCD justification.

cost: Free to build and to list. Charging merchants through an App Store app must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API, and Shopify takes a revenue share (not verified here).

paths.name: Custom distribution
paths.who_for: One specific merchant (an agency client, or your own store) or multiple stores in a single Shopify Plus organization
paths.limits: One store, or stores in one Plus org. Installed by a generated install link. The distribution method can't be changed later, so you'd need a new app to go public. Not listed in the App Store. Level 1 and Level 2 protected customer data are available without review.

paths.name: Public distribution (Shopify App Store listing)
paths.who_for: An AI-agent product where any merchant can connect their store
paths.review: App Store review (automated checks plus human review), and protected customer data review if requested
paths.limits: Before approval, installs work only on development stores. Installs must be initiated from Shopify (App Store URL or Shopify-managed install). Needs a merchant-facing UI, compliance webhooks, expiring offline tokens, Billing API for charges and GraphQL Admin API for new apps.

paths.name: Store-owned app (created inside a merchant's organization in Dev Dashboard)
paths.who_for: A merchant building an internal integration for their own store
paths.limits: Replaces legacy admin-created custom apps, which can't be created after Jan 1, 2026. Can use the client credentials grant for stores in its own organization. Not a multi-tenant option.

prerequisites.item: Shopify Partner account (free) with access to the Dev Dashboard at dev.shopify.com
prerequisites.note: Sign up and 2FA. Partner Dashboard data has been migrated into Dev Dashboard.

prerequisites.item: Shopify CLI 3.84.1+ and Node.js (if building with the app template)
prerequisites.note: Needed to deploy config (scopes, compliance webhooks) via shopify.app.toml

prerequisites.item: Public HTTPS app URL and redirect URL(s)
prerequisites.note: Valid TLS cert required for App Store
Created from the Dev Dashboard. Can be created on any plan, including Plus.

prerequisites.item: Privacy policy URL, support contact, emergency developer contact
Data protection answers and security controls for Level 2 PCD (encryption, access logs, incident response policy, etc.)
prerequisites.note: Only if you need customer name/email/phone/address

steps.title: Create a Partner account and open the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Sign up at partners.shopify.com and open dev.shopify.com/dashboard. Apps, stores, payouts and org settings now live there. App listings, pricing and review still live in the Partner Dashboard until distribution moves to Dev Dashboard.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Option A: `shopify app init` (React Router template) then `shopify app dev`. This uses Shopify-managed installation plus token exchange, and expiring offline tokens via `future: { expiringOfflineAccessTokens: true }`. Option B: Dev Dashboard > Apps > Create app for a standalone or API-only agent backend that uses the authorization code grant. Copy the Client ID and Client secret.

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect URLs in shopify.app.toml
steps.detail: Under [access_scopes] set `scopes` to the minimum needed (e.g. read_products,read_orders). Avoid read_all_orders unless justified. Under [auth] set `redirect_urls`. These must exactly match the redirect_uri you send. Deploy with `shopify app deploy` to release a version.

steps.title: Declare mandatory compliance webhooks
steps.detail: In shopify.app.toml add [webhooks] api_version plus [[webhooks.subscriptions]] with compliance_topics = ["customers/data_request","customers/redact","shop/redact"] and a uri. Verify X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 and return 401 on bad HMAC (the community reports the automated checker also accepts 400). Respond 2xx, and complete the action within 30 days. These are no longer set in the dashboard UI. Runtime subscriptions don't satisfy the checker.

steps.title: Choose the distribution method (irreversible)
steps.detail: Dev Dashboard > your app > Home > Distribution card > Select distribution method. Custom: enter the merchant's myshopify.com domain, toggle multi-store for a Plus org, then Generate link. Public: you'll create an App Store listing. 'You can't change the method after you select it.'

steps.title: Request protected customer data access (if agent touches customer PII)
steps.detail: Partner Dashboard > Apps > your app > API access requests > Protected customer data access > Request access. Select 'Protected customer data' (Level 1) with reasons, then select individual fields (Name, Email, Phone, Address = Level 2) with reasons, then complete Data protection details. On dev stores this unlocks immediately. Public apps need review. This also covers customer-related data on orders, so agent workflows over orders usually need at least Level 1.

steps.title: Install on a dev store and obtain an expiring offline token
steps.detail: Authorize: https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&redirect_uri=...&state=.... On callback, verify hmac and state, and validate shop against ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$. Then POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token with client_id, client_secret, code, expiring=1. Store access_token (expires_in 3600) and refresh_token (refresh_token_expires_in ≈ 90 days).

steps.title: Build the App Store requirements (public only)
steps.detail: Requirements: OAuth immediately on install, before any UI, then redirect to the app UI. A UI is required even for backend or agent apps, embedded in the admin with the latest App Bridge and session tokens that work without third-party cookies. New public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API and expiring offline tokens. Charges go through the Billing API or App Pricing, including upgrade, downgrade and reinstall handling. Run the AI self-review checklist or Dev MCP before you submit.

steps.title: Create listing and submit
steps.detail: Listing: name, icon, screenshots, pricing details, privacy policy URL. The submission needs a demo screencast (English or subtitled) of onboarding and core features, and test credentials that bypass 2FA/SSO and stay valid after publish. Set an emergency developer contact. Make sure automated checks pass, then submit.
steps.wait: Officially up to ~2 weeks. 2026 community reports: 2–5+ weeks.

steps.title: Publish and handle token refresh at scale
steps.detail: After approval, merchants install from the App Store URL. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token per shop. Serialize refreshes per shop, save the new access/refresh pair atomically, and always use the newest refresh token. Handle 401 on uninstall (subscribe to app/uninstalled).

review.trigger: Public distribution, so any merchant outside one store or Plus org can install, needs App Store review. Requesting protected customer data on a public app adds PCD review (Level 1 or Level 2). Custom distribution and dev-store-only use need no review.
review.process: Submit from the Partner Dashboard listing. Automated checks run first (compliance webhooks, HMAC verification, OAuth-on-install, etc.), then a human reviewer installs the app on a test store using your screencast and credentials. Feedback comes by email and in the dashboard. Fix and resubmit; resubmitting puts you at the back of the queue. Apps that repeatedly fail may be temporarily suspended from submitting.
review.typical_wait: Confirmation email says up to 2 weeks. Shopify staff acknowledged longer-than-usual times in Feb 2026, and community threads report 2–5+ weeks through Oct 2026.
reviewers_check: OAuth happens immediately after install and reinstall, before any UI interaction (2.3.2/2.3.4)
App has a functional merchant UI, embedded in the admin with current App Bridge (2.1.3, 2.2.3)
Embedded app works without third-party cookies or local storage, e.g. in Chrome incognito (session tokens, 1.1.1)
Mandatory compliance webhooks are declared in config and verify HMAC
All charges go through the Shopify Billing API or App Pricing, with plan changes working (1.2.x)
Minimal scopes, with justification for sensitive ones like read_all_orders (3.2)
Expiring offline access tokens used (3.1.2), valid TLS (3.1.1), GraphQL Admin API for new apps (2.2.4)
Screencast, working test credentials, accurate listing with no unsubstantiated claims (4.x)
Protected customer data use matches stated purpose; Level 2 security controls
common_rejections: Automated check fails: 'Provides mandatory compliance webhooks' and 'Verifies webhooks with HMAC signatures', because topics were subscribed at runtime instead of in shopify.app.toml, or bad HMAC wasn't rejected
Install flow not initiated from Shopify, or UI shown before OAuth
Off-platform billing (Stripe checkout etc.) instead of the Billing API
Test credentials missing, expired or behind 2FA
Requesting scopes or protected fields not clearly needed by visible features
Backend-only/headless app with no meaningful merchant UI

pre_approval_limits: Before approval, a public app can only be installed on development stores; merchant installs are blocked
Custom distribution: one store, or stores in one Plus organization, permanently for that app
Protected customer data fields on unreviewed public apps work only on development stores
Partner Dashboard CLI tokens expire by Feb 6, 2027. Switch CI to SHOPIFY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN.

oauth.refresh_tokens: Only for expiring offline tokens, requested with expiring=1. The refresh token lasts ~90 days from issue (refreshing can shorten it) and rotates on use. Since Aug 2026 an already-used refresh token can be retried for up to 30 days, until the replacement is used. Online tokens have no refresh token; get a new one by re-running token exchange. Legacy non-expiring offline tokens can be migrated with token exchange (subject_token_type=urn:shopify:params:oauth:token-type:offline-access-token, expiring=1), which permanently invalidates the old token for GraphQL.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: Expiring offline: 1 hour (expires_in 3600). Online: 24 h or until the user logs out of admin. Non-expiring offline (legacy): no expiry, but rejected with 403 for existing public apps after Jan 1, 2027, and not allowed for public apps created on or after Apr 1, 2026.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must exactly match one of the redirect_urls in the Dev Dashboard or the [auth] section of shopify.app.toml. HTTPS expected (CLI tunnels used in dev). Validate hmac, state, shop and timestamp before exchanging code.
oauth.scopes: Comma-separated access scopes like read_products, write_orders, read_customers. read_all_orders (beyond 60 days) needs justification. Protected customer data is a separate permission layer. Level 1 covers customer data excluding identifying fields. Level 2 adds per-field Name, Email, Phone, Address and needs extra security controls and review for public apps. Optional scopes can be dynamically granted and revoked.
oauth.tenant_notes: Every store is a separate tenant with its own hostname, so all OAuth and API URLs are per shop ({shop}.myshopify.com) and tokens are per app per shop. Shopify keeps one current expiring offline token per app+shop; getting a new one retires older ones after their expiry. Embedded CLI apps use Shopify-managed installation (scopes from toml) plus token exchange of the App Bridge session token (id_token) for online or offline tokens. Uninstall revokes all tokens and gives 401.

gotchas.title: Distribution method is permanent
gotchas.detail: Picking Custom distribution for a quick pilot means you need a brand-new app (new client_id, every merchant reinstalls) to go public later.

gotchas.title: Customer PII needs a separate protected customer data approval
gotchas.detail: Agents that read customer names, emails, phones or addresses (including on orders) need Level 2 PCD. Without it, those fields are redacted or error even if you hold read_customers. It works on dev stores, so it often surprises teams only at production.

gotchas.title: Expiring offline tokens are mandatory for new public apps
gotchas.detail: Public apps created on or after Apr 1, 2026 must send expiring=1 and refresh hourly. Existing public apps lose non-expiring tokens on Jan 1, 2027 (403). Your library must implement per-shop serialized refresh with atomic storage.

gotchas.title: App Store apps must have a merchant UI and use Shopify Billing
gotchas.detail: A pure backend agent connector isn't permitted. 'All apps in the Shopify App Store must be operational through a UI.' Off-platform charging isn't allowed.

gotchas.title: Review backlog in 2026
gotchas.detail: Shopify staff acknowledged longer review times in Feb 2026. Community threads report 2–5+ weeks, and resubmitting moves you to the back of the queue.

gotchas.title: Compliance webhooks must be declared in config, not at runtime
gotchas.detail: The automated checker reads compliance_topics from the released app version. Subscribing via API after install fails the check.

gotchas.title: Strict shop hostname validation
gotchas.detail: Use an anchored regex. An unanchored check lets exampleshop.myshopify.com.attacker.example receive the code.

gotchas.title: Legacy admin custom apps are gone
gotchas.detail: Merchants can no longer create admin custom apps with pre-generated tokens (since Jan 1, 2026). Old tutorials telling users to 'Develop apps > Create an app' in admin are outdated.

gotchas.title: Refresh-token anomalies have occurred
gotchas.detail: In July 2026 refresh tokens were issued with ~1 second expiry, which Shopify fixed after reports. Log request IDs and treat refresh failures as recoverable for the 30-day window.

blockers.symptom: Merchant sees an error installing your public app before approval
blockers.cause: Unapproved public apps can only install on development stores, and installs must start from Shopify
blockers.fix: Use dev stores until approved, or ship a separate custom-distribution app for a pilot merchant

blockers.symptom: Automated check failed: 'Provides mandatory compliance webhooks' / 'Verifies webhooks with HMAC signatures'
blockers.cause: compliance_topics not in the released shopify.app.toml, or invalid HMAC not rejected
blockers.fix: Add [[webhooks.subscriptions]] compliance_topics, run shopify app deploy, return 401 on bad HMAC, then rerun checks

blockers.symptom: Customer fields null or access-denied errors for email/phone/address on a production store
blockers.cause: Protected customer data (Level 2 fields) not approved for public app
blockers.fix: Partner Dashboard > API access requests > Protected customer data access; select fields, complete data protection details, submit for review

blockers.symptom: 403 on GraphQL Admin API after Jan 1, 2027 with an old token
blockers.cause: Non-expiring offline token on a public app
blockers.fix: Migrate with token exchange (expiring=1) before the deadline, or make merchants re-authenticate

blockers.cause: redirect_uri not exactly in [auth] redirect_urls of the released version
blockers.fix: Add the URL to shopify.app.toml and shopify app deploy

agent_can: scaffold the app with Shopify CLI and write shopify.app.toml (scopes, redirect_urls, compliance webhooks)
implement OAuth with HMAC, state and shop validation and expiring-token refresh
draft protected customer data justifications and data-protection answers
run the AI self-review checklist or Dev MCP against the codebase
draft listing copy, privacy policy and screencast script
create dev stores and test installs
human_must: sign up for a Partner account and complete 2FA
attest to security controls for Level 2 PCD
provide test credentials and an emergency contact
click Submit for review and respond to reviewer emails
set up payout and tax details if charging

evidence.note: Migration permanently invalidates the old token for GraphQL Admin API requests

uncertain: Exact current App Store review SLA; only 'up to 2 weeks' (confirmation email) and community reports of 2–5+ weeks
Protected customer data review duration, which isn't published
Shopify revenue share percentage on app charges, not verified in this pass
Whether every App Store app must be embedded, versus just having a UI integrated into admin; requirements text is ambiguous
Exact date distribution and listing management move from Partner Dashboard to Dev Dashboard ('soon')
PKCE: not mentioned in the Shopify auth-code-grant docs reviewed; marked 'not supported' because the documented flow is confidential-client only
Whether the automated HMAC checker expects 401 (official docs) or 400 (community fix); returning 401 per docs is the safe default

probes.result: Authorize URL is per-shop ({shop}.myshopify.com); needs a dev store, which requires creating an account — out of scope for an automated agent.
